items.title: REGN 2-DAY DEADLINE ALERT: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Investors Alerted to September 14, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline in Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals over allegations that the company made false and misleading statements regarding a Phase 3 clinical trial of Fianlimab for melanoma treatment. The trial failed to reach statistical significance on its primary endpoint, causing an $11 billion market cap loss. Investors claim Regeneron concealed flawed statistical assumptions and slow event rates while expressing confidence in the trial's success. The lead plaintiff deadline is September 14, 2026.

items.title: BioNTech vs. Moderna: Which Is the Better Cancer Vaccine Stock to Buy Now?
items.summary: BioNTech and Moderna, both mRNA vaccine pioneers during the pandemic, are now pivoting to cancer vaccines as COVID revenue declines. Moderna is favored due to stronger recent clinical progress, including positive phase 3 results for its personalized cancer vaccine intismeran autogene and FDA approval for mFLUSIVA flu vaccine. While BioNTech has a deep pipeline including pumitamig, it has yet to deliver comparable phase 3 wins. Moderna's $61.2 billion market cap reflects investor confidence in its near-term commercialization prospects versus BioNTech's $26 billion valuation.

items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway shifted to net stock buying in Q2 2026 under CEO Greg Abel, purchasing $39.4 billion in equities during the first half of the year compared to $7.1 billion a year earlier. The company's most notable addition was Alphabet, making it the third-largest portfolio position. Despite a frothy market with elevated valuations, Abel is playing offense while managing $365.5 billion in cash and Treasuries awaiting deployment.

items.title: VEEV Raises FY27 Outlook as Vault CRM and AI Momentum Accelerate Fast
items.summary: Veeva Systems raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $3.682-$3.687B (implying ~15% growth), driven by strong Vault CRM adoption with commitments from 12 of top 20 biopharma firms and 180+ live customers. The company's Falcon AI product has five early adopters, though execution remains a key near-term priority. While profitability is maintained with a 44% operating margin, newer initiatives like CRM migrations and AI monetization still require sustained execution.

items.title: The Market Just Told You Which Layer Of AI Biology It Is Paying For
items.summary: Recent earnings in life sciences technology reveal that the market is rewarding companies with proprietary data and systems of record over those selling software or AI models alone. Veeva Systems beat expectations with strong AI product adoption, while Certara missed on modest software growth and Recursion Pharmaceuticals fell short on revenue expectations. MindWalk Holdings, which owns curated biological data infrastructure, is positioned to benefit from this trend with its HYFT Technology and newly launched ReefIQ platform, though it remains unprofitable with modest recurring revenue.

items.title: Why Palo Alto Networks Stock Jumped 15% In August Before Falling This Week
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks stock surged 15% in August driven by strong demand for cybersecurity solutions amid AI threats, but fell over 10% this week after reporting Q4 earnings with disappointing fiscal 2027 guidance of 23-24% revenue growth. The stock trades at a premium P/S ratio of 22x, requiring investors to believe in sustained 20%+ growth and significant margin expansion to justify current valuations.

items.title: Old Dominion Unveils Solid LTL Unit Performance for August

items.title: Stock Market Midday, Sept. 3: Stocks Rally as Treasury Yields Fall, Broadcom Falls Despite Earnings Beat
items.summary: U.S. stock markets rallied on September 3, 2026, as Treasury yields fell and the probability of a September rate hike decreased. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled a preference for holding rates steady unless inflation surprises emerge. The S&P 500, Dow Jones, and Nasdaq all gained over 1%, with industrials and financial services leading. Notable movers included Snowflake surging 20% on strong earnings, while Broadcom declined despite beating expectations. Nvidia gained on news of acquiring AI platform Hugging Face.

items.title: Equinix, NVIDIA & Together AI Accelerate Enterprise AI Inference
items.summary: Equinix has partnered with NVIDIA and Together AI to launch Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference platform for enterprises. The solution combines NVIDIA's Enterprise Reference Architectures, Together AI's inference capabilities, and Equinix's global infrastructure to enable faster, more cost-efficient AI deployment across multiple geographies. The platform will support metro-edge inference, open-source models, and sovereign AI requirements, with availability expected in Q1 2027.

items.title: Does Moderna's mRNA Flu Shot Face a New Challenge From GSK?
items.summary: Moderna secured FDA approval for mFlusiva, the first mRNA-based seasonal flu vaccine, establishing a foothold in the multibillion-dollar flu vaccine market. However, GSK announced plans to advance its own mRNA flu vaccine into phase III trials, which targets two viral proteins (HA and NA) and showed superior immune responses in phase II studies. While GSK's vaccine is still years away from market approval, it could pose a competitive challenge to Moderna's mFlusiva, which currently targets only HA like traditional flu vaccines.

items.title: Tim Cook's Legacy at Apple Will Be Defined by This Nearly $879 Billion Investment, Not AI

The deal extends Vertiv's capabilities across the full power value chain from grid to chip, including microgrid solutions and on-site generation, enabling faster time-to-power for data center developers.

items.title: Where Will SoundHound AI Stock Be in 1 Year?
items.summary: SoundHound AI, trading near its 52-week low of $7, is predicted to rise approximately 25% over the next year. The company has experienced significant revenue growth from under $50 million to an expected $237 million this year, driven by expansion beyond automotive into restaurants, hospitality, and customer service. The pending acquisition of LivePerson could push combined 2027 revenue to $350-400 million, potentially justifying higher valuations if the company continues to perform well.

items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited, alleging the company misrepresented and failed to disclose its ties to China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), which classifies it as a Chinese military company under the NDAA. Additionally, Alibaba allegedly conducted fraudulent 'distillation attacks' against Anthropic's Claude AI models using fake accounts. The stock declined following these revelations in June 2026, and investors who suffered losses between June 26, 2025, and June 24, 2026, are urged to contact the law firm by October 5, 2026.

The lawsuit alleges the company made materially false statements about its financial health and channel inventory, particularly in its Pool segment. On July 14, 2026, Pentair shocked investors with a massive revenue miss ($930M vs. $1.14B forecast), revealed $170M in inventory destocking impacts, slashed full-year guidance, and announced an abrupt CFO departure. The stock plummeted 15% the following day.

items.title: Sandisk Stock: Buy, Sell, or Hold?
items.summary: Sandisk stock has quintupled year-to-date and appears poised for further gains as Samsung's announcement of multiyear memory chip deals with Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet through 2031 intensifies the memory shortage. Sandisk is growing faster than Samsung (372% vs 130% YoY revenue growth) and securing similar long-term contracts, providing revenue visibility and pricing power. With a 77% net profit margin and only a 20 P/E ratio, the company is well-positioned to capitalize on sustained AI-driven demand for memory chips.

items.title: Sysco's Fiscal 2027 Outlook Puts AI Cost Savings in the Spotlight
items.summary: Sysco Corporation projects fiscal 2027 sales growth of 6-7% to ~$90B and adjusted EPS growth of 9-11%, driven by AI-enabled productivity initiatives expected to deliver $100M in cost savings. However, the company's outlook depends on stable restaurant traffic and modest inflation, with execution risk around converting planned savings into sustained margin expansion while continuing infrastructure investments.

items.title: Quanta's Net Income Nearly Doubles: Can Profit Growth Stay Hot?
items.summary: Quanta Services (PWR) reported exceptional Q2 2026 results with net income nearly doubling to $451.4 million and revenues climbing 41.1% to $9.56 billion. The Electric segment led growth with 43.6% revenue increase and 62.5% operating income surge. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for net income to $1.74-$1.82 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $4.09-$4.21 billion, supported by strong infrastructure demand and recent acquisitions.

items.title: Dell's $95 Billion Backlog Answers the AI Question
items.summary: Dell Technologies posted record quarterly revenue of $46.97 billion (58% YoY growth) with non-GAAP EPS of $7.04 (203% YoY growth), significantly beating consensus estimates. The company booked a record $60.9 billion in AI server orders and exited with a $95 billion backlog. Dell raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $192 billion from $167 billion, implying 69% growth. Gross margins expanded 260 basis points to 20.9%, disproving concerns that AI servers carry structurally lower margins. Growth extended beyond AI servers, with traditional servers up 122% and storage up 26%.

items.title: Berkshire's Biggest New Position Came From Warren Buffett, Not From Greg Abel

The lawsuit alleges that Pentair made materially false statements regarding its business operations, specifically failing to disclose significant inventory destocking in the Pool channel that adversely affected sales and operating income. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 2, 2026.

EquipmentShare investors who purchased stock during its January 2026 IPO through June 23, 2026 can seek lead plaintiff status by September 21, 2026. The lawsuit alleges the company failed to disclose material information including undisclosed related party transactions and misleading financial statements. Capricor Therapeutics investors have until September 28, 2026 to apply.

items.title: INV SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed on Behalf of Innventure, Inc. Investors - Contact Kirby McInerney LLP by October 27, 2026
items.summary: Kirby McInerney LLP has filed a securities fraud class action lawsuit against Innventure, Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Innventure made materially false statements regarding a transformative deal with DarkNX for an AI data center in Ontario, Canada, and overstated revenue and cash flow targets for its subsidiary Accelsius Holdings LLC. Following a May 28, 2026 Morpheus Research report questioning the deal's existence, and Innventure's August 13, 2026 disclosure that the deployment site was no longer available, the stock price fell 55% to $1.62 per share. The deadline to request lead plaintiff appointment is October 27, 2026.

items.title: GDDY SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed on Behalf of GoDaddy Inc. Investors - Contact Kirby McInerney LLP by October 20, 2026
items.summary: Kirby McInerney LLP has filed securities fraud class action lawsuits against GoDaddy Inc., Taboola.com Ltd., and Innventure, Inc. on behalf of investors. The GoDaddy lawsuit alleges the company failed to disclose that a $4.99 promotional pricing strategy for one-year domain contracts would materially impact bookings growth, which fell to 5% in Q4 2025, causing the stock to drop 14% on February 24, 2026. Investors have until October 20-27, 2026 to request lead plaintiff appointment.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Sept. 1: Intel Falls on Chip Stock Pressure
items.summary: Intel closed down 0.60% at $88.97 on September 1, 2026, as higher Treasury yields and inflation concerns pressured semiconductor stocks broadly. The decline was driven by macro factors rather than company-specific issues, with peers like AMD and Qualcomm also falling. Intel's recent $20 billion equity offering and progress in reducing foundry business losses provide some optimism, though near-term volatility is expected as investors assess whether Intel can maintain its position in the AI market.

items.title: Nvidia Sells the Brains of the AI Boom. Something Else Is Selling the Muscle -- and It's Not on Wall Street's Radar.
items.summary: While Nvidia dominates AI chip sales, an overlooked opportunity exists in 800-volt power distribution equipment for data centers. This technology offers ~10% cost savings over conventional power supplies and is being developed by companies like Vertiv and Nvidia. Though the transition could take years given the industry's $700 billion annual AI infrastructure spending, this emerging sector presents significant long-term potential.

items.title: Amazon Doesn't Pay a Dividend and Constantly Dilutes Shareholders. Here's Why I'd Still Buy and Hold It Forever.
items.summary: The article argues that Amazon is a compelling long-term buy despite not paying dividends and diluting shareholders through equity compensation. The author contends that Amazon's powerful Prime ecosystem (valued at $1,430 annually vs. $139 cost), expanding rural logistics network, and strategic AI investments through AWS and partnerships with Anthropic create an unassailable competitive moat. Rather than returning cash to shareholders via dividends, Amazon reinvests profits into infrastructure and innovation, positioning it as a compounding growth machine.

items.title: Vertiv Plunges 20% in Three Months: Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Vertiv shares fell 20% in three months due to project delays and supply-chain issues, but the company reported strong Q2 results with 24% sales growth and 22.6% adjusted operating margin. Benefiting from robust AI infrastructure demand, Vertiv expects Q3 sales of $3.65B-$3.85B and adjusted EPS of $1.77-$1.83. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (20.94X Price/Book) and faces stiff competition, earning a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Eni Builds Uruguay Offshore Presence Through New Exploration Deals
items.summary: Eni has signed agreements to expand its presence in Uruguay's offshore exploration sector. The Italian energy company will operate the OFF-5 block with MIWEN (YPF subsidiary) holding 50%, and will acquire a 40% stake in the neighboring OFF-6 block operated by APA Corporation. Eni will fund a significant portion of an initial exploration well scheduled for 2027. These moves strengthen Eni's position in Latin America and diversify its upstream operations.

items.title: I've Been Wrong About Philip Morris International Stock for 5 Years. Here's Why I'm Finally Changing My Mind.
items.summary: The author reverses his 5-year bearish stance on Philip Morris International after the company successfully pivoted from declining cigarettes to higher-margin smoke-free products. Smoke-free products now represent 42% of revenue (up from 24% in 2020), with strong growth in IQOS heated tobacco and ZYN nicotine pouches. Q2 results beat expectations with 10.4% revenue growth and 15.2% EPS growth. However, at current valuations near $192, the stock is no longer considered cheap despite the improved business fundamentals.

items.title: Amazon vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Amazon and Shopify as investment options for 2026. Amazon dominates with $716.9B in revenue and a 10.8% net margin but faces regulatory scrutiny and plans $200B in capex spending for AI infrastructure. Shopify, growing at 30.1% annually with zero debt and $2B in free cash flow, is positioned as the higher-growth, lower-risk alternative. The author recommends Shopify for investors seeking high rewards with relatively low risk.

items.title: JSAIY vs. WMT: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: A comparison of J. Sainsbury PLC (JSAIY) and Walmart (WMT) as value investment options reveals that JSAIY is the superior choice. JSAIY has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 14.50 and Value grade of A, while WMT has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 36.51 and Value grade of D. JSAIY's lower valuation metrics and improving earnings outlook make it more attractive for value investors.

items.title: Sundar Pichai Says Alphabet's AI Overviews Now Reach 2.5 Billion Monthly Users as Ad Revenue Hit $82 Billion. Does That Scale Justify Spending Up to $205 Billion on AI Infrastructure This Year?
items.summary: Alphabet is investing up to $205 billion in AI infrastructure in 2026, building on $91 billion spent in 2025. The company's AI initiatives have reached 2.5 billion monthly users through Google Search's AI Overviews and generated $82 billion in ad revenue. Google Cloud revenue surged 82% year-over-year to $25 billion in Q2 2026. Despite taking on $114 billion in debt, Alphabet maintains positive free cash flow of $53 billion over the trailing 12 months, positioning it competitively ahead of peers like Amazon and Meta in the AI infrastructure race.

items.summary: Broadcom is expected to report Q3 fiscal 2026 results on September 2 with revenues of ~$29.4 billion (84% YoY growth) and AI semiconductor revenues accelerating to ~$16 billion (200%+ YoY growth). However, gross margin pressure from lower-margin AI semiconductors and stretched valuation present headwinds. The stock has underperformed peers despite strong AI momentum with major customers including Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta.

items.title: Netflix Is Down 46% From Its High. Is This a Once-in-a-Lifetime Buying Opportunity Before the Stock Goes Parabolic?
items.summary: Netflix stock has fallen 46% from its all-time high amid revenue growth deceleration, but the company maintains strong profitability with a 33.4% operating margin and is executing on key initiatives including ad-tier expansion (250M+ users), live programming (NFL, WWE), and a $25 billion share buyback program. While not a 'once-in-a-lifetime' opportunity, the stock at 19-22x 2026 earnings represents reasonable valuation for a maturing business with solid long-term fundamentals.

items.title: Nebius vs. CoreWeave: Which Is the Better Artificial Intelligence (AI) Infrastructure Stock to Buy Right Now
items.summary: Nebius and CoreWeave are neocloud infrastructure companies benefiting from surging AI data center demand, with the market expected to grow at a 58% CAGR through 2031. Nebius has outperformed with 146% gains in 2026 and improving profitability, while CoreWeave trades cheaper but faces higher losses despite a stronger revenue backlog of $104 billion. Both stocks offer long-term growth potential depending on investor risk profile.

items.title: Lowe's Cuts 2026 Outlook as DIY Pressure Tests Its Growth Engines
items.summary: Lowe's beat Q2 earnings expectations with $4.40 EPS but missed revenue forecasts and significantly lowered fiscal 2026 guidance to flat comparable sales and $12.25 EPS. While Pro, Online, and Home Services segments showed strength with 15.7% online sales growth, weak DIY demand, housing pressures, and margin headwinds from fuel, transportation, and competitive pricing drove the cautious outlook reset.

items.title: Stryker to Acquire ZuriMED to Expand Its Shoulder Care Portfolio
items.summary: Stryker announced a definitive agreement to acquire ZuriMED, developer of the FiberLocker System for rotator cuff augmentation. The acquisition aims to strengthen Stryker's shoulder portfolio and expand its rotator cuff repair capabilities in sports medicine and arthroplasty. Despite the strategic move, SYK shares fell 2.1% following the announcement, though the global rotator cuff repair market is projected to grow at 7.6% CAGR through 2033.

The company plans to develop the location into a liquid asphalt terminal to improve sourcing and transportation across Oklahoma and North Texas. items.title: Prediction: Amazon Could Be Worth This Much in 5 Years
items.summary: Amazon is expected to outperform the broader market over the next five years, driven by strong growth in its cloud computing segment (AWS) and AI investments. The article projects Amazon's stock could reach approximately $460 by 2031, representing a 12% annualized return, assuming 12% annual earnings growth and stable valuation multiples. Key growth drivers include AWS's 37% year-over-year revenue growth, internally developed AI chips improving margins, and productivity gains in e-commerce.

items.title: Buy 5 AI-Powered Momentum Stocks for September After a Strong August
items.summary: U.S. stock markets surged in August driven by renewed AI enthusiasm, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite advancing 2.6% and 3.9% respectively. Five AI infrastructure leaders—NVIDIA, Super Micro Computer, Semtech, SiTime, and Keysight Technologies—all holding Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) ratings with momentum scores of A, are expected to maintain their upward trajectory. NVIDIA's data center revenue jumped 117% year-over-year to $89 billion, while Semtech projects 160% year-over-year data center growth in Q3.

items.title: Here's How Much You'd Have If You Invested $1000 in Synopsys a Decade Ago
items.summary: A $1,000 investment in Synopsys (SNPS) made in September 2016 would have grown to $7,414.24 by September 2026, representing a 641.42% gain—significantly outperforming the S&P 500's 254.05% return. The company benefits from recurring revenue, strong demand for chip design and AI-related tools, and the Ansys acquisition expansion, though elevated debt and execution risks remain concerns.

items.title: Nvidia Just Proved It Doesn't Need China Anymore
items.summary: Nvidia provided fiscal 2028 guidance forecasting 70% revenue growth, significantly exceeding Wall Street's 44% expectations. The company demonstrated it can achieve substantial growth without relying on China, where it now generates less than 1% of data center revenue. With a forward P/E of 23 and PEG ratio of 0.6, Nvidia appears undervalued despite its accelerating growth trajectory.

While the increased engine supply relieves supply-chain bottlenecks and benefits aircraft manufacturers' revenues and margins, it creates near-term margin pressure for GE Aerospace as new engine sales are typically lower-margin compared to lucrative long-term aftermarket service agreements.

items.title: C3.ai vs. Oracle: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Investment in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares C3.ai and Oracle as AI investment options. C3.ai, focused on enterprise AI software, experienced a 35.7% revenue decline in FY2026 and posted a net loss of $470.4 million, though it maintains a strong balance sheet with zero debt. Oracle, an AI infrastructure provider, grew revenue 17.4% to $67.4 billion with a 25.4% net margin and $638 billion in remaining performance obligations. The author recommends Oracle as the stronger investment due to consistent revenue growth and future guidance of $90 billion in FY2027 sales, while C3.ai must prove it can recover from recent challenges.

items.title: Why Hormel Foods Stock Swooned by 10% Today
items.summary: Hormel Foods stock plummeted 10% after the company missed revenue expectations ($2.96B vs. $3.05B consensus), cut full-year net sales guidance to $12.1-$12.2B from $12.2-$12.5B, and reported a 7% drop in sales volume. While the company beat earnings per share estimates ($0.37 vs. $0.35 consensus), investors were unforgiving due to weak consumer demand, lower commodity-based pricing, and the company's already-eroded stock performance.

items.title: Deadline Alert: Pentair plc (PNR) Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP About Securities Fraud Lawsuit
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Pentair plc for allegedly failing to disclose significant inventory destocking in its Pool channel between March and July 2026. The company's undisclosed issues led to a 15% stock price drop on July 15, 2026, when it revealed that destocking negatively impacted Pool segment sales by $170 million. Investors who purchased Pentair securities during the class period have until October 2, 2026 to file a lead plaintiff motion.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Aug. 27: Salesforce Surges 23% on Anthropic Partnership and Q2 Earnings Beat
items.summary: Salesforce stock surged 22.6% on August 27, 2026, following a strong Q2 earnings beat, raised full-year guidance, and announcement of a new AI partnership with Anthropic to develop Claudeforce. The company reported 11% sales growth and 14% growth in remaining performance obligations, while agentic workforce units grew 97%. Peers ServiceNow and Workday also gained on broad enterprise software enthusiasm.

items.title: BABA INVESTOR ALERT: Alibaba Group Holding Limited Investors with Substantial Losses Have Opportunity to Lead Shareholder Class Action Lawsuit Before October 5, 2026 Deadline – RGRD Law
items.summary: Robbins Geller announces a class action lawsuit against Alibaba Group Holding Limited for alleged securities violations. The lawsuit claims Alibaba made false statements about its control by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and engaged in unauthorized AI model distillation attacks. The stock declined following disclosure of Alibaba's inclusion on the U.S. Department of Defense's Chinese military companies list and Anthropic's accusations of illicit AI model access. Investors with substantial losses can seek appointment as lead plaintiff before October 5, 2026.

items.title: The Stock Market Is Giving Investors a Second Chance to Buy This Incredible AI Chip Stock
items.summary: Qualcomm is presented as an attractive buying opportunity following a semiconductor sector sell-off in July 2026. The company is positioned to benefit from AI adoption in mobile devices through its Snapdragon chips and has ambitious plans to generate $15 billion in data center revenue by 2029, with deals already in place with hyperscalers and Meta. Despite near-term headwinds from rising memory prices and Apple dropping its baseband chips, the stock trades at a reasonable 15.3x forward earnings multiple.

items.title: I Think Johnson & Johnson Is the Best Dividend Stock to Buy Right Now
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson is highlighted as an excellent dividend stock choice due to its 64-year streak of consecutive annual dividend increases, making it a Dividend King. With a diversified portfolio spanning Innovative Medicine and MedTech segments, 28 billion-dollar product platforms, and strategic investments in oncology, immunology, and robotic surgery, J&J offers stable, growing cash payouts backed by a resilient healthcare business. The company raised 2026 guidance and continues to innovate while maintaining a ~2% dividend yield.

items.title: PENTAIR CLASS ACTION ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C. Encourages Pentair plc Investors to Contact the Firm Seeking Lead Plaintiff Role Before October 2nd
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Pentair plc for allegedly failing to disclose significant inventory destocking in its Pool channel between April 28, 2026 and July 14, 2026, which adversely affected sales and operating income. The company's positive statements about its business and prospects are alleged to be materially misleading. Investors who purchased Pentair securities during the class period have until October 2, 2026 to apply for lead plaintiff status.

items.title: Dan Ives Says the AI Trade Is Only in the "Third Inning." Should Investors Stay Long AI Stocks?
items.summary: Dan Ives argues the AI revolution is still in early stages, comparing it to the third inning of baseball. The focus is shifting from GPU purchases to monetizing AI across infrastructure, cloud platforms, and software. Companies with real AI revenue, clear ecosystem roles, and strong customer bases are positioned best for long-term growth.

items.title: Why ServiceNow Rallied Today
items.summary: ServiceNow stock rallied 9.2% following Salesforce's strong earnings report, which alleviated fears of a 'SaaS-pocalypse' from agentic AI. Salesforce reported 10.8% revenue growth, beat EPS estimates by 80%, and showed its AI-infused Agentforce features growing at 210% annualized revenue run rate. Both companies are positioned as platforms that will collaborate with AI rather than be disrupted by it, with Salesforce announcing a partnership with Anthropic called 'Claudeforce.'

items.title: Securities Fraud Investigation Into XTI Aerospace, Inc. (XTIA) Announced – Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz
items.summary: XTI Aerospace announced on August 17, 2026, that it could not timely file its Form 10-Q due to an internal review of its former CEO who resigned, along with other corporate governance matters. The stock fell 15.9% to $1.32 on August 18, 2026. A securities fraud investigation has been initiated on behalf of investors who lost money.

items.title: Stryker to participate in the 2026 Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference
items.summary: Stryker announced its participation in the 2026 Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference on September 8, 2026, with CFO Preston Wells and VP of Investor Relations Nick Mead participating in a fireside chat. The company also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.88 per share and reported second quarter 2026 operating results with net sales increasing 9.4% to $6.6 billion.

items.title: Why Dollar General Stock Is Up Today
items.summary: Dollar General's stock rose 3.08% after the retailer boosted its full-year profit forecast. The company reported 5.2% net sales growth to $11.3 billion in Q2, driven by store openings and 3.5% same-store sales growth. Higher gas prices are pushing consumers to seek bargains closer to home, benefiting Dollar General's 21,000+ store network. The company raised its full-year same-store sales guidance to 2.5%-2.9% and EPS guidance to $7.80-$8.00, and plans a $700 million stock buyback.

items.title: Nvidia $100 Billion Historic Quarter Confirms the AI Boom
items.summary: Nvidia delivered extraordinary Q2 results with 106% YoY revenue growth to $96.2B, 75% gross margins, and $59.7B net income. The company is compared to historical capital-goods suppliers during major investment booms. Unlike the dot-com era's dark fiber overbuild, AI infrastructure appears economically justified with high utilization rates and profitability. At 23.5x forward earnings with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), NVDA stock appears attractively valued despite risks from concentrated customer base and massive financing requirements.

items.title: Allstate Stock: Strong Earnings and Growth Keep the Outlook Bright
items.summary: Allstate Corporation (ALL) is well-positioned for growth driven by improving underwriting profitability, rising investment income, and solid policy growth. The company reached 216 million policies in force in Q2 with a 9.9% increase in issued applications. Net investment income surged 33.8% to $1 billion in Q2, while the company repurchased $1 billion in stock. ALL trades at a valuation discount with a forward P/E of 8.73X versus its five-year median of 10.90X and has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

items.title: Best Buy Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates as Comparable Sales Rise 4.1%
items.summary: Best Buy (BBY) delivered better-than-expected second-quarter fiscal 2027 results with adjusted earnings jumping 70.1% to $1.48 per share and revenues rising 3.6% to $9.78 billion. Domestic comparable sales grew 4.5%, driven by computing, mobile phones, and services. The company raised its full-year fiscal 2027 guidance for revenues, comparable sales, earnings, and adjusted operating margins, citing strong first-half performance and positive momentum.

items.title: Hormel Foods Q3 Earnings Beat on Margin Expansion, Sales Miss
items.summary: Hormel Foods reported Q3 adjusted EPS of 37 cents, beating consensus estimates, but net sales fell 2.4% to $2.96B, missing expectations. The company expanded operating margins by 60 basis points despite volume declines across segments. Hormel lowered fiscal 2026 sales guidance to $12.1-$12.2B but raised EPS guidance to $1.45-$1.51, reflecting a Brazil divestiture and challenging external environment.

items.title: DLTR Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates on Margin Gains and Higher Comps
items.summary: Dollar Tree (DLTR) posted solid Q2 fiscal 2026 results with net sales rising 7% to $4.89B and adjusted EPS climbing 80.5% to $1.39, beating consensus estimates. Gross margin expanded 850 basis points to 42.9%, driven by tariff refunds and lower tariff rates. The company raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.70-$8.05 while maintaining its sales outlook of $20.5-$20.7B.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Insulet Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Insulet Corporation alleging that the company made materially false and misleading statements regarding its business operations and compliance policies. The complaint specifically claims that Insulet's manufacturing controls were defective, creating a foreseeable risk that products could violate safety regulations. Investors who purchased Insulet securities between May 21, 2025 and May 26, 2026 are encouraged to join the lawsuit, with a lead plaintiff deadline of August 31, 2026.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Pentair plc Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Pentair plc alleging that company executives made materially false statements and failed to disclose significant inventory destocking in the Pool channel that adversely affected sales and operating income during the period of April 28, 2026 to July 14, 2026. Investors who purchased Pentair securities during this period are encouraged to join the lawsuit, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 2, 2026.

items.title: HPE vs. CSCO: Which Stock Has an Edge in the Networking Space?
items.summary: HPE and Cisco are competing for enterprise and data center networking spending driven by AI demand. HPE strengthened its position through the Juniper acquisition with 148% networking revenue growth, while Cisco benefits from $9.3 billion in hyperscaler AI orders and strong data center momentum. Despite HPE's superior year-to-date performance (130% vs. 45.9%), Cisco is rated as the more compelling investment due to its stronger competitive position, diversified portfolio, and operating leverage, though both carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

items.title: VIRT vs. MCO: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: In a value investing comparison, Virtu Financial (VIRT) emerges as the superior choice over Moody's (MCO). VIRT holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) with a forward P/E of 9.36 and Value grade of B, while MCO has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 30.47 and Value grade of D. VIRT's lower valuation metrics and stronger earnings outlook make it the better value opportunity.

items.title: Is Quanta Becoming the Biggest Winner From America's AI Buildout?
items.summary: Quanta Services (PWR) is emerging as a major beneficiary of AI-driven infrastructure expansion, with a record $53.4B backlog supported by utility generation, transmission, and technology load center projects. The company's recent acquisitions and joint venture are expected to add $1.2-$1.4B in 2026 revenues and $120-$140M in EBITDA. PWR's ability to self-perform 80-85% of its work positions it well to capture growing infrastructure investment opportunities.

items.title: HON vs. EMR: Which Automation Stock Has Better Growth Potential?
items.summary: Honeywell Technologies and Emerson Electric are compared as industrial automation leaders. HON faces near-term headwinds from weak Process Automation demand, rising costs, and elevated debt ($31.5B), though Building and Industrial Automation segments show strength with 9% and 4% organic revenue growth respectively. EMR demonstrates broader momentum with 6% underlying sales growth, strength across power, LNG, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets, and strategic acquisitions enhancing its AI and software capabilities. Despite HON's Strong Buy rating, EMR appears the better investment choice given stronger recent stock performance, improving earnings outlook, and healthier end-market demand.

items.title: Greg Abel Has Kept 60% of Berkshire's $359 Billion Stock Portfolio in Just 5 Companies, Even After Eliminating 16 Other Positions in His First Quarter. Is That Concentration a Risk for Shareholders?
items.summary: Since becoming CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, Greg Abel has maintained high concentration in five blue-chip stocks (Apple, American Express, Alphabet, Bank of America, and Coca-Cola), which now represent 60% of the portfolio. While this concentration is largely inherited from Warren Buffett's long-term investments, the article argues that downside risk is manageable given Berkshire's strong financial position. The greater concern is whether Abel can match Buffett's stock selection track record going forward.

items.title: Veeva Systems Q2 Earnings and Revenues Beat Estimates, Stock Up
items.summary: Veeva Systems (VEEV) reported Q2 fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $2.35, up 18.1% YoY and beating consensus by 5.9%, with revenues rising 17.6% to $928 million. The company raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $3.682-$3.687 billion and EPS to $9.21. Vault CRM momentum continued with over 180 customers live including five top 20 biopharmas, while the company advanced its AI strategy with Veeva Falcon.

items.title: Seagate (STX) Up 10.7% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Seagate reported Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings of $5.71 per share, beating estimates of $5.10, with revenues of $3.6 billion up 48% year-over-year. Strong AI-driven demand for cloud storage and robust enterprise OEM demand drove 34% revenue growth to $12.2 billion for fiscal 2026. The company expects fiscal 2027 revenue growth to outpace 2026, with Q1 2027 guidance pointing to $4.1 billion in revenues and $7.3 EPS. Seagate has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating with upward estimate revisions of 30.61%.

items.title: Sherwin-Williams (SHW) Up 1.4% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Sherwin-Williams reported Q2 2026 earnings that beat estimates with adjusted EPS of $3.70 (up 9.5% YoY) and revenues of $6.79 billion (up 7.5% YoY). All three segments showed growth, supported by the Suvinil acquisition. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for both net sales and earnings. However, management expects demand softness to continue in the second half. The stock has gained 1.4% since the earnings report but underperformed the S&P 500, and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Coca-Cola (KO) Up 1.1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Coca-Cola reported strong Q2 2026 results with EPS of 97 cents (up 11% YoY) and revenues of $13.38 billion (up 7% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. The company raised its 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 5% and comparable earnings growth to 9-10%. However, estimates have trended downward since the earnings release, and the stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by about 1.1% over the past month.

items.title: KLA (KLAC) Up 8% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: KLA (KLAC) reported fiscal Q4 2026 earnings of $1.05 per share, beating estimates by 5%, with revenues of $3.66 billion up 15.2% year-over-year. The company benefited from AI infrastructure investment and strong foundry/logic demand. KLA issued strong Q1 FY2027 guidance of $4 billion in revenues and raised its calendar 2026 wafer fabrication equipment market outlook to the low-$150 billion range. The stock has received a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with upward estimate revisions.

items.title: Procter & Gamble Has Raised Its Dividend for 70 Straight Years. Here's How Much $25,000 Invested Pays Annually.
items.summary: Procter & Gamble has maintained 70 consecutive years of annual dividend increases, making it one of only two companies with such a long streak. A $25,000 investment would generate approximately $750 in annual dividend income at the current 3% yield. While the yield is modest, P&G's dividend has grown at an annualized rate of 4.8% over the past decade, outpacing inflation and rewarding patient long-term investors.

items.title: Why Palo Alto Networks Stock Just Popped
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks stock surged 11.1% on reports the cybersecurity company is shifting into acquisition mode. After failed attempts to acquire Okta and Datadog at lower valuations, Palo Alto is now targeting smaller companies Cribl and ClickHouse for potential acquisition.

items.title: Can JPMorgan's Stablecoin Push Strengthen Its Digital Payments Edge?
items.summary: JPMorgan is exploring a stablecoin offering that would extend its digital payments strategy through its JPM Coin and Kinexys platforms. The initiative could enable 24/7 settlement, improve liquidity management, and create fee opportunities. JPMorgan's established blockchain infrastructure gives it a competitive advantage over Bank of America and Wells Fargo, which are still evaluating their digital-dollar strategies. Regulatory clarity could further improve the economics of such an initiative.

items.title: Why the Summer Slump is Setting Up Wall Street's Next Rally
items.summary: Technical analysis shows QQQ is positioned for a rally, with historical data indicating positive returns following eight consecutive down closes. Bearish sentiment has reached extreme levels for six consecutive weeks, a contrarian indicator that preceded a multi-week rally in April. NVIDIA exceeded Wall Street expectations with $96.2B in revenue and announced significant capacity expansion plans for Neocloud partners, signaling strength in the AI sector.

items.title: Amphenol (APH) Recently Broke Out Above the 50-Day Moving Average
items.summary: Amphenol (APH) is displaying bullish technical indicators after breaking above its 50-day moving average and reaching key support levels. The stock has gained 7.3% over the past four weeks and holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating. Positive earnings estimate revisions, with no downward revisions in the past two months and five upward revisions, further support the bullish outlook.

items.title: HPQ Q3 Earnings Call Puts Focus on Margin Recovery & AI PCs
items.summary: HP Inc. raised its fiscal 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $3.19-$3.29 and free cash flow to $3-$3.2B, driven by pricing discipline, premium PC mix, and strong AI PC adoption at 46% of Q3 shipments. The company expects Personal Systems margins to bottom in Q4'26 before improving in FY27 through mitigation actions including product redesign and supplier optimization. Print segment margins remained strong at 18.1% despite a 2% revenue decline.

items.title: Forget Bloom Energy Stock at $207 Per Share. Buy This Hydrogen-Focused ETF Instead for Just $43.
items.summary: While Bloom Energy has surged 321% over the past year with strong 2026 guidance, its valuation has become stretched at 18.5x sales and 265x earnings. The article recommends the Global X Hydrogen ETF (HYDR) at $43 as a more prudent alternative, offering diversified exposure to Bloom Energy and other hydrogen industry players like Plug Power and FuelCell Energy.

items.title: MP Materials vs. Enterprise Products: Which "Boring" Business Actually Has the Better Growth Case?
items.summary: MP Materials and Enterprise Products Partners both demonstrate strong revenue growth, but offer different investment profiles. MP Materials, a rare-earth miner backed by DoD funding, shows 89% YoY revenue growth and is approaching profitability, while Enterprise Products Partners offers stable, diversified revenue streams with a well-covered 5.66% dividend and 28 consecutive years of dividend increases. The article concludes Enterprise Products Partners is the better investment due to more stable revenue and lower risk.

items.title: Uber Stock Is 20% Off Its All-Time High, While the S&P 500 Index Is Up 14% Since Then: Here's Why the Market's Bearish View Is Wrong.
items.summary: Uber shares have fallen 20% from their all-time high while the S&P 500 has risen 14%, driven by investor concerns about autonomous vehicle technology disrupting its business model. However, the author argues this bearish view is unwarranted, citing Uber's strong financial performance (24% gross bookings growth, 13.3% operating margin), massive user base of 208 million monthly active users, powerful network effects, and strategic partnerships with AV companies. The author contends that a hybrid model of human drivers and self-driving vehicles will likely coexist, and Uber's matching technology and geographic diversification position it well to compete.

With capital expenditures of $195-205 billion planned for 2026, the company's cash generation is running behind its AI ambitions, making shareholders net funders rather than beneficiaries.

Investors who purchased Pentair securities between April 28, 2026 and July 14, 2026 may be eligible for compensation, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 2, 2026.

items.title: INTU Stock News: Robbins LLP Reminds Investors of the Pending Lead Plaintiff Deadline in the Intuit Inc. Securities Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A securities class action has been filed against Intuit Inc. for allegedly misleading investors about its business sustainability and growth prospects, particularly regarding its TurboTax operations. The lawsuit claims Intuit failed to disclose increasing competitive and pricing pressures in its tax business. The stock declined significantly following announcements of a 17% workforce reduction and disappointing Q3 2026 financial results on May 20-21, 2026. The deadline to seek lead plaintiff appointment is September 8, 2026.

items.title: I Think Johnson & Johnson Is the Best Dividend Stock to Buy Right Now
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson stands out as an attractive dividend stock due to its diversified healthcare business, strong financial health with an AAA credit rating, impressive 64-year dividend increase streak, and recent progress in resolving talc-related lawsuits. Despite patent cliffs and drug price negotiations, the company expects 6.8% revenue growth for fiscal 2026, demonstrating resilience.

items.title: Microsoft Earns 31% More Than It Did a Year Ago and Is Worth Less
items.summary: Microsoft reported strong fiscal 2026 results with net income up 31% to $133.7 billion and revenue up 18% to $331.8 billion. However, its market cap declined 4.5% year-over-year as investors reassessed the company's valuation from 37x to 27x earnings. The primary concern is Microsoft's massive capital expenditure surge to $175 billion for calendar 2026, which now exceeds its operating income, raising questions about the return on investment for AI infrastructure spending.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals alleging that the company made materially false and misleading statements regarding its Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo study. The complaint claims the study's preliminary statistical assumptions were flawed, the treatment arm lacked meaningful clinical differentiation, and the study was unlikely to achieve statistical significance. Investors who purchased Regeneron securities between August 1, 2025 and May 15, 2026 are eligible to join the case.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alibaba Group Holding Limited Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited alleging securities fraud violations. The lawsuit claims that Alibaba made materially false and misleading statements regarding its business operations and prospects, specifically related to alleged control by the Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and ongoing distillation attacks against third-party AI models. The class period covers purchases between June 26, 2025 and June 24, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 5, 2026.

items.title: Micron Technology Has Fantastic News for Memory Stock Investors
items.summary: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra states that AI infrastructure demand has fundamentally changed the memory industry from cyclical to structural growth. Data center memory demand exceeds supply by 50%, with additional demand from autonomous vehicles and edge AI devices. Recent memory stock sell-offs present attractive buying opportunities as the sector is poised for long-term growth.

items.title: Axon Enterprise vs. Booking Holdings: Evaluating Absolute Scale and Sequential Volatility in Quarterly Revenue Trends
items.summary: Axon Enterprise demonstrates consistent quarter-over-quarter revenue growth with a 6% operating margin, while Booking Holdings generates significantly larger absolute revenue but exhibits cyclical fluctuations with a 34% operating margin. Axon trades at a higher P/E ratio (253.98) due to its leadership in law enforcement technology and expanding software services, whereas Booking trades lower (23.64) due to slower growth and competitive pressures. The article examines whether Axon can maintain high growth and narrow the gap with Booking, or if Booking's 'Connected Trip' strategy will accelerate its revenue expansion.

items.title: Marvell Technology's Next Earnings Report on Aug. 27 Could Send the Stock Soaring. Here's Why.
items.summary: Marvell Technology is expected to report Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings on Aug. 27 with significant market expectations. The company recently announced a $12.2 billion custom chip deal with Google for AI inference hardware, which could generate up to $120 billion in revenue over seven years. Investors will focus on management's forward guidance for fiscal 2027-2028 to assess the deal's impact. While positioned as a critical 'picks-and-shovels' player in AI infrastructure, Marvell's high valuation (83x trailing P/E) leaves little room for disappointment.

items.title: Kaplan Fox Encourages GoDaddy Inc. (NYSE: GDDY) Investors with Significant Losses to Contact the Firm Before October 20, 2026
items.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a class action lawsuit against GoDaddy Inc. alleging the company made false and misleading statements about its customer growth strategy during September 2025 through February 2026. The company allegedly implemented promotional discounts on short-term contracts that caused bookings growth to decelerate to 5% in Q4 2025, which was not disclosed to investors. The stock price fell 14% (from $92.30 to $79.12 per share) on February 25, 2026 following the disclosure of the true financial results.

items.title: mRNA Therapeutics Market Outlook Report 2026-2035 Featuring Profiles of Arcturus Therapeutics, BioNTech, CureVac, Moderna, Providence Therapeutics, RNAimmune, Recode Therapeutics, and More
items.summary: The global mRNA therapeutics market (excluding COVID-19 applications) is projected to grow from USD 201 million in 2026 to USD 9.98 billion by 2035, with a 63% CAGR. Growth is driven by expanding oncology and rare disease pipelines, advances in lipid nanoparticle delivery, and strategic partnerships. However, challenges include tissue-selective delivery limitations, repeat-dose tolerability concerns, and regulatory complexities. Moderna and BioNTech dominate with approximately 70% of pipeline activity.

items.title: Greg Abel Just Made 3 Moves at Berkshire Hathaway That Bet on the Same Trend (And it's Not AI)
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway CEO Greg Abel is making significant bets on a housing market recovery through multiple moves: acquiring homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $8.5 billion, increasing investment in Lennar by 30%, and buying shares of D.R. Horton. These moves, combined with existing holdings in Clayton Homes and Berkshire Hathaway Home Services, suggest Abel believes pent-up demand will emerge once mortgage rates decline, despite the currently frozen housing market.

items.title: History Says What the 2025 Auto Tariffs Cost General Motors, and Canada's Rate Is About to Double
items.summary: President Trump announced tariffs on Canadian vehicles will rise to 50% on January 1, 2027, doubling the current 25% rate. However, GM's stock showed muted reaction as the company has demonstrated resilience in the previous tariff cycle, absorbing $3.1 billion in costs against a $5 billion forecast and offsetting over 40% through pricing and manufacturing adjustments. GM has also reduced its Canadian footprint and raised profit guidance twice in 2026.

items.summary: A class action securities lawsuit has been filed against EquipmentShare.com Inc. (EQPT) for allegedly failing to disclose material information in its January 2026 IPO registration statement and during the subsequent class period. The company and its executives are accused of concealing undisclosed related party transactions with co-founder-controlled entities and providing materially misleading financial statements. Investors who purchased shares between January 23, 2026 and June 23, 2026 may be eligible to participate, with a September 21, 2026 deadline to request lead plaintiff status.

items.title: This $30 Stock Could Be Primed for a Breakout
items.summary: Applied Digital (APLD), an AI data center company trading near $30, shows impressive 407% revenue growth but remains unprofitable. While the company benefits from surging AI demand with projected 127% revenue growth in FY 2028, its lack of profitability and high valuation of 13x sales present significant risks. The stock's performance is heavily tied to AI market sentiment, making it volatile and potentially riskier than other AI investments.

items.title: Monster Beverage's 2-for-1 Stock Split Is Now Complete. Here's What Comes Next for Investors.
items.summary: Monster Beverage completed its 2-for-1 stock split on August 11, 2026, with the stock climbing about 5% since the split. While the company has a high forward P/E ratio of 41.6, it demonstrates strong fundamentals including 21.6% growth in core energy drink sales, robust international expansion (46% of Q2 sales), and long-term opportunities in the alcohol segment. The stock is recommended for aggressive investors seeking long-term growth, though conservative investors may find the valuation and lack of dividends unappealing.

items.title: EQPT DEADLINE NOTICE: ROSEN, A HIGHLY RECOGNIZED LAW FIRM, Encourages EquipmentShare.com Inc Investors with Losses in Excess of $100K to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - EQPT
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is notifying investors in EquipmentShare.com Inc, ARS Pharmaceuticals Inc, and Barclays PLC of ongoing securities class action lawsuits. EquipmentShare investors who purchased shares during the IPO or within the Class Period are encouraged to join the lawsuit, with a lead plaintiff deadline of September 21, 2026. The lawsuits allege material misstatements and omissions regarding business operations and financial disclosures.

items.title: Alpha Metallurgical Director Courtis Keeps Buying as He Adds Another  $1.1 Million Shares
items.summary: Kenneth S. Courtis, a director at Alpha Metallurgical Resources, purchased 5,000 shares for $1.1 million on August 25, 2026, marking his third major buy in a week totaling over $7 million. Despite industry headwinds including rising operational costs and declining coal demand, Courtis's continued insider buying signals confidence in a potential turnaround, though the company reported a $46.1 million net loss on $2.1 billion in revenue.

items.title: Alibaba Group Holding Limited (BABA) Investors: Securities Fraud Class Action Filed, Contact Hagens Berman Before October 5, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline
items.summary: A securities fraud class action has been filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited, alleging the company misrepresented its ties to China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and concealed unauthorized access to third-party AI models. The lawsuit covers the period from June 26, 2025 to June 24, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 5, 2026. Alibaba's stock fell approximately 4-5% following regulatory disclosures in June 2026.

items.title: Alphabet Investors Are Still Underestimating Google Cloud
items.summary: Google Cloud's revenue growth has accelerated dramatically from 32% year-over-year in Q2 2025 to 82% in Q2 2026, outpacing AWS and Azure. Driven by AI workload demand and higher compute pricing, Google Cloud's operating income more than tripled and now represents 21.6% of Alphabet's total profits, with potential to reach 50% within 2-3 years if growth continues.

items.title: Pomerantz Law Firm Announces the Filing of a Class Action Against Insulet Corporation and Certain Officers – PODD
items.summary: Pomerantz LLP filed a class action lawsuit against Insulet Corporation (PODD) for alleged securities fraud. The complaint alleges that Insulet made false statements about its manufacturing controls and failed to disclose defective procedures that created safety risks. Two voluntary medical device corrections were announced in March and May 2026, resulting in significant stock price declines of 6.88% and 5.07% respectively. Investors who purchased Insulet securities between February 21, 2025 and May 26, 2026 can join the class action.

items.title: Oklo Isn't Exactly an AI Stock. Here's Why I Love It Anyway.
items.summary: Oklo, a small modular reactor (SMR) nuclear energy company, is positioned to benefit from massive AI industry electricity demands. With $7 trillion expected to be spent on data center infrastructure, nuclear energy is experiencing renewed interest as an ideal clean power solution. Oklo differentiates itself by marketing directly to AI companies rather than utilities, and has already secured deals with Meta. However, the company remains speculative pending regulatory approval and real-world demonstration of its technology.

items.title: 1 Reason Home Depot's 17-Year Dividend Streak Makes It a Buy This Week
items.summary: Home Depot faces near-term headwinds from higher mortgage rates, inflation, and a sluggish housing market, resulting in modest 1.7% same-store sales growth. However, the article argues patient investors should consider buying the stock for its attractive 2.74% dividend yield, supported by 17 consecutive years of annual dividend increases. The company is positioned to benefit when economic conditions improve and homeowners resume major renovation projects.

items.title: Sundar Pichai Says Alphabet's AI Products Now Reach Over 2.5 Billion Monthly Users Through AI Overviews. Here's What That Scale Means for Ad Revenue Investors.
items.summary: Alphabet announced that its AI Overviews reach over 2.5 billion monthly users, with AI Mode serving 1 billion active users. Google Search advertising revenue grew 16.7% year-over-year to $63.27 billion in Q2, while total advertising revenue reached $81.63 billion, up 14%. The company is investing heavily in AI infrastructure with $44.9 billion in capital expenditures, supported by Google Cloud revenue growth of 82% to $24.8 billion.

items.title: Dell Technologies vs. UiPath: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Dell Technologies and UiPath as investment options in 2026. Dell dominates hardware infrastructure with $113.5B in FY2026 revenue and benefits from surging AI server demand, but carries $31.5B in debt. UiPath, a smaller AI automation software company with $1.6B revenue, recently achieved profitability with a 17.5% net margin and zero debt. The author concludes Dell is the better choice due to its massive scale, profitability, and explosive AI server growth projections of $60B+ in FY2027.

items.title: Nebius Group N.V. vs. SoundHound AI: Which AI Stock Will Bring You Profits in 2026 and Beyond?
items.summary: Nebius Group and SoundHound AI represent two different approaches to AI investment: Nebius focuses on infrastructure with 350% revenue growth and achieved profitability in 2025, while SoundHound offers voice AI solutions with 100% revenue growth but remains unprofitable. Nebius carries higher valuation risk and capital intensity, while SoundHound faces legal challenges and competitive threats from tech giants. The article suggests Nebius may be the better choice if investors believe in AI's long-term potential and can justify its high valuation.

items.title: Jensen Huang Told Investors in Seoul to "Buy at a Discount" During the Recent AI Stock Sell-Off. Here's Whether His Call Has Paid Off.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang advised investors to 'buy at a discount' during a June tech stock sell-off when Nvidia shares had fallen 13%. Since then, Nvidia stock has gained 2.2%, underperforming the S&P 500's 3.1% gain. However, the stock remains reasonably valued with forward P/E ratios of 23.8x (fiscal 2027) and 16.5x (fiscal 2028), as Wall Street has also raised earnings expectations. Nvidia's strong free cash flow of $48.6 billion and dominant position in AI infrastructure support its valuation, though the call's success ultimately depends on upcoming earnings results.

items.title: BABA Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Alibaba Group Holding Limited Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law
items.summary: Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP announces a securities fraud class action lawsuit against Alibaba Group Holding Limited for allegedly making false and misleading statements regarding its control by the Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information and undisclosed AI model distillation activities. The class period spans June 26, 2025 to June 24, 2026, with a deadline of October 5, 2026 for investors to participate.

items.title: PNR Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Pentair plc Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law
items.summary: Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP has filed a class action lawsuit against Pentair plc for alleged securities violations under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The lawsuit claims Pentair made false and misleading statements regarding a significant destocking event in its Pool channel that negatively impacted sales and income. The class period runs from April 28, 2026 to July 14, 2026, with a deadline of October 2, 2026 for investors to participate.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Investors
items.summary: The Portnoy Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals on behalf of investors who purchased securities between August 1, 2025 and May 15, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Regeneron made false statements about its Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo clinical trial, concealing risks and flawed statistical assumptions. The trial ultimately failed to reach statistical significance on its primary endpoint, causing Regeneron's stock to drop approximately 10% on May 15, 2026.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of Insulet Corporation Investors
items.summary: The Portnoy Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit on behalf of Insulet Corporation investors who purchased securities between February 21, 2025 and May 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Insulet made false statements regarding defective manufacturing controls and failed to disclose the full scope of safety issues with its Omnipod insulin pump products. Two voluntary medical device corrections were announced in March and May 2026, resulting in stock price declines of 7% and 5% respectively. Investors have until August 31, 2026 to file a lead plaintiff motion.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of Intuit, Inc. Investors
items.summary: The Portnoy Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Intuit Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased securities between August 22, 2025 and May 20, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Intuit made false statements about its competitive advantages and business strength, while concealing significant losses in its TurboTax business due to competitive pressures. On May 20, 2026, news of a 17% workforce reduction and weak Q3 2026 tax revenue guidance (7% growth vs. 8% consensus) caused Intuit's stock to drop over 20%. The deadline to file a lead plaintiff motion is September 8, 2026.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of GPGI, Inc. Investors
items.summary: The Portnoy Law Firm has announced a class action lawsuit on behalf of GPGI, Inc. investors who purchased securities between November 3, 2025 and May 6, 2026. The lawsuit follows two major stock price declines triggered by disappointing earnings reports and significant guidance cuts. In March 2026, GPGI's stock fell 16.36% after reporting compressed EBITDA margins at its Husky Technologies segment. In May 2026, the stock plummeted an additional 25.89% following weak Q1 results and substantial downward revisions to full-year guidance.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of Futu Holdings Limited Investors
items.summary: Futu Holdings Limited faces a class action lawsuit alleging the company made false statements about its compliance with China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) requirements. The company allegedly conducted securities, public fund sales, and futures business in mainland China without proper licenses. On May 22, 2026, Futu disclosed a CSRC notification proposing penalties totaling approximately RMB1.85 billion (~$271 million), causing the stock to fall over 27%. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased securities between May 24, 2023 and May 27, 2026.

items.title: BE Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Bloom Energy Corporation Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE) for alleged securities violations. The company is accused of making false and misleading statements regarding its sourcing of scandium, which was actually sourced from China through middlemen while the company understated its reliance on Chinese scandium. The class period runs from February 27, 2025 to July 8, 2026, with a deadline of September 28, 2026 for investors to participate.

items.title: AI in Patient Engagement Market Size to Reach USD 45.90 Billion by 2035 as Healthcare Automation Accelerates – SNS Insider
items.summary: The global AI in Patient Engagement Market is projected to grow from USD 7.85 billion in 2025 to USD 45.90 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 19.34%. Growth is driven by widespread adoption of conversational AI, virtual health assistants, predictive analytics, and remote patient monitoring. North America leads with 38.50% market share, while Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region at 23.80% CAGR. Natural Language Processing dominates technology segment with 39.80% share, and cloud deployment accounts for 64.20% of the market.

items.title: State of the Life Sciences Industry to Be Reviewed in BCC Research's 2026 Second Quarter Outlook, Spotlighting AI-Driven Discovery, Precision Oncology, and Connected Health Adoption
items.summary: BCC Research's mid-year assessment highlights AI-driven discovery, precision oncology, and connected health as major growth themes in the life sciences sector. Key opportunities include smart inhalers with AI integration, genomic profiling platforms, cardiovascular drug innovations, and in vitro toxicity testing. The sector benefits from aging populations, regulatory support for non-animal testing, and emerging market expansion, though risks include patent expirations and reimbursement variability.

items.title: Pure Cycle Corporation Appoints Two Industry Leaders, Chris Fink and Kelly Haecker, to its Board of Directors
items.summary: Pure Cycle Corporation announced the appointment of Chris Fink and Kelly Haecker as independent directors to its Board of Directors, effective August 24, 2026. Fink brings four decades of municipal finance experience from Bank of America Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley, while Haecker brings public company CFO experience from WhiteWave Foods and currently serves as a partner at Capitol Peak Partners. The appointments return the Board to eight directors, seven of whom are independent.

items.title: Confidential Computing Market to Reach $1,425.71 Billion by 2035 as Data-in-Use Security and AI Adoption Surge | Research by SNS Insider
items.summary: The global confidential computing market is projected to grow from $17.37 billion in 2025 to $1,425.71 billion by 2035, at a CAGR of 55.39%. Growth is driven by increasing demand for data-in-use security, AI adoption, and enterprise workload protection. North America leads with 40.50% market share, while Asia Pacific shows fastest growth. Software & Services dominates by component, though Hardware is the fastest-growing segment at 67.10% CAGR.

items.title: CapEx Finance Index July 2026: Demand Surges on AI Investment
items.summary: The Equipment Leasing & Finance Association reported record-breaking demand in July 2026, with seasonally adjusted new deal volumes reaching $14.3 billion, 24.5% above the previous all-time high. AI-related investment drove the surge, with the full-year 2026 forecast now projected at $137.3 billion, surpassing 2024's record by 14%. Credit quality improved with loss rates at nine-month lows, though industry risks have shifted from demand concerns to rising funding costs as the Fed signals potential rate hikes.

items.title: 6G Radio Revenue to Reach US$67 Billion by 2034 as Operators Face AI Infrastructure Crossroads
items.summary: ABI Research forecasts 6G radio revenue will grow from $8.1 billion in 2029 to $67.0 billion in 2034, with AI-chipset radio revenue scaling from $1.8 billion to $57.7 billion over the same period. Telecom operators face a critical 2026-2028 investment window to decide whether to remain connectivity providers or expand into distributed AI infrastructure and new revenue models. The 2029-2031 period will be key for validating enterprise demand and AI monetization models.

items.summary: Navitas Semiconductor announced a definitive agreement to acquire Claros, Inc., a power management solutions company, for approximately $232.8 million. The acquisition aims to complete Navitas' grid-to-xPU power delivery portfolio by combining Claros' vertical power delivery (VPD) and integrated voltage regulator (IVR) technologies with Navitas' GaN and SiC semiconductors. The deal is expected to more than double Navitas' 2030 serviceable addressable market to over $8 billion and accelerate its AI infrastructure strategy.

items.title: Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Will Be Worth More than SpaceX Before 2026 is Over
items.summary: The article argues that Meta Platforms will likely surpass SpaceX in valuation by the end of 2026. Meta currently trades at a low 17.5x forward earnings compared to the S&P 500's 21.4x, while SpaceX is valued at nearly 40x sales despite generating no net income. Meta's $15.8 billion quarterly profit dwarfs SpaceX's $7.8 billion revenue, suggesting Meta's valuation is more justified and has room to grow.

Cruz is investigating Hims & Hers Health, Inc. following an FTC lawsuit alleging deceptive privacy practices and unauthorized sharing of customers' medical information with third-party advertisers like Meta and Snap. Additionally, Visa placed Hims on its Acquirer Monitoring Program due to excessive customer complaints and credit card disputes in its weight-loss subscription business, resulting in significant surcharges. These developments caused substantial stock price declines.

items.title: U.S. FDA Grants Orphan Drug Designation to Gamgertamig for the Treatment of Pemphigus
items.summary: Lakefront Biotherapeutics announced that the FDA has granted Orphan Drug Designation to gamgertamig for treating pemphigus, expanding on previous Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations for autoimmune hemolytic anemia and immune thrombocytopenia. The drug, developed in collaboration with Gilead Sciences, is currently in Phase 1b trials with expansion anticipated in 2027 and registrational studies expected in 2027.

items.summary: Kimberly-Clark is an overlooked Dividend King with a 54-year consecutive dividend increase streak matching PepsiCo's. Despite lower brand recognition, KMB offers a higher yield (4.7% vs 4.1%), more resilient demand for household products, and is acquiring Kenvue to enhance its global portfolio, making it an attractive option for income-focused investors.

items.title: Is MP Materials Stock a Buy After Earnings?
items.summary: MP Materials reported strong Q2 earnings with 89% revenue growth to $108 million and a swing to $28.5 million adjusted EBITDA. The company is shifting from selling low-value rare earth concentrate to higher-margin separated NdPr oxide and metal products, with concentrate revenue dropping to zero while oxide/metal revenue jumped to $95 million. While the stock is down 45% from its 52-week high, the company's improving economics and Pentagon partnership support a cautiously optimistic outlook, though scaling magnet production remains a key test.

items.title: Jeff Bezos' Amazon Just Raised Its AI Spending Target to $220 Billion for 2026. Here's What That Capex Hike Means for Investors.
items.summary: Amazon increased its 2026 capital expenditure target to $220 billion, citing higher memory chip costs. Despite the increased spending, Amazon's revenue growth (20% YoY) outpaces capex growth, with AWS achieving its highest growth rate in over four years. Operating income surged 43.2% YoY to $27.5 billion in Q2, with AWS contributing $16.6 billion. The massive capex investment reinforces Amazon's dominant position in cloud computing and creates barriers to entry for competitors.

items.title: A Lumentum Executive Sold 2,000 Shares Under a Plan He Filed in May. Here's What to Know
items.summary: Wupen Yuen, president of global business units at Lumentum Holdings, disposed of 12,565 shares totaling $10.7 million on August 19-20. The majority (84%) consisted of shares withheld for tax obligations from restricted stock vesting, while 2,000 shares were sold under a pre-planned Rule 10b5-1 trading plan filed in May. Despite the sales, Yuen maintains a significant 93,229-share position. The transaction occurs as Lumentum reports strong growth with components revenue up 103% and total revenue up 109% year-over-year, driven by demand for near-packaged optics technology for AI applications.

items.title: What to Know About the CFO of Lumentum's Latest Insider Transaction Filing
items.summary: Lumentum's CFO Ali Wajid sold 10,728 shares worth $9.1 million on August 19-21 to satisfy tax withholding obligations from vesting equity awards, reducing his direct holdings by 13%. Despite the paper loss from convertible bond conversions, the company's underlying business showed strong performance with revenue up 109% year-over-year and operating margins improving to 36.6%.

items.title: Lumentum's CEO Parted With 6,185 Shares in August. Here's What Long-Term Investors Should Know
items.summary: Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston sold 6,185 shares worth $5.1 million on August 19 to cover tax withholding obligations from restricted stock unit vesting. This was a non-discretionary transaction and does not reflect his view on the stock. Hurlston retains 112,794 shares valued at $93.35 million. The stock has delivered a 602% one-year return, and the company is guiding for $1.25 billion in September quarter revenue with 39.5-40.5% margins, hitting its target model early amid strong demand for optical and photonic products.

items.title: The One Line in Anthropic's S-1 That Amazon Investors Should Read First
items.summary: Anthropic is expected to file its S-1 for an IPO by month-end, potentially matching SpaceX's record raise. The AI lab is valued at $965 billion with quarterly revenue exceeding $11.5 billion. Amazon has invested $13 billion in Anthropic with commitments for up to $20 billion more, and the partnership is deepened through AWS infrastructure and custom silicon usage. Anthropic's S-1 disclosure will clarify Amazon's ownership stake and could lead to a fundamental rerating of Amazon stock as investors better understand Anthropic's impact on AWS revenue and AI infrastructure growth.
